key_concepts: Homeostasis is a self-regulating process that maintains stability
Feedback mechanisms are loops where output enhances or inhibits production
Negative feedback counteracts changes from a set point
Negative feedback is the most common homeostatic mechanism
Positive feedback amplifies changes away from the initial state
Feedback loops involve receptors, control centers, and effectors
Body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure are homeostasis indicators
Endocrine organs such as pancreas and thyroid help regulate homeostasis
Childbirth, blood clotting, and lactation are positive feedback examples
Stimulus, receptor, and control center have specific roles in feedback
